content:
maria: Heads-up — preparing a modular rollout for the gpu/vpc/iam modules. planning to split the big gpupool module into gpupool-core + gpupool-net so we can iterate on KMS/IAM without touching capacity. want feedback on compatibility approach.

sam: +1 on splitting. question: are we going to pin the provider and module versions in the root live repo or rely on the module's go.mod style pin? last infra incident was provider drift.

leo: I'd strongly prefer pinning at the root's module ref. we should create a compatibility shim for the old tfstate names to avoid costly state mv during canary. shim = small module that maps old resources to new addresses via aliases.

zara: worried about KMS changes — when we rework kms bindings we risk encrypt key policy mismatch in eu-west1. we had a customer workload hit because kms key is org-scoped and the new module tries to create a regional alias. need a safe plan.

maria: plan proposal: 1) cut gpupool-core v0.1.0 (no KMS/IAM) 2) cut gpupool-net v0.1.0 (VPC, subnets) 3) canary release to us-west1 only, 5% of new autoscale groups, 24h soak 4) then apply gpupool-kms v0.1.0 with *no* replace — only creates new resources, doesn't touch existing key bindings 5) if stable, roll out full region.

sam: how will gitops pipeline handle the multiple modules? our argo app currently references a single module ref.

leo: we add a new overlay kustomize/argocd app that points to the staged module refs. pipeline: PR -> terratest -> plan comment -> manual approve -> canary apply. deploy-bot will post plan results.

maria: example plan snippet I expect in canary:
```
# module.gpupool-core.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_asg will be created
+ resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_asg" {
    + name = "gpu-asg-usw1-canary"
    + desired_capacity = 4
    ...
}
# module.gpupool-kms.aws_kms_key.k main will NOT be replaced (no changes)
```

leo: also add a migration job to run state rm/state mv if we detect unmigrated addresses. but that must be manual and only after a green canary.

zara: cost note: switching to gpupool-core split may temporarily increase API calls and double some resources during canary — estimate +8-12% spend for 48h. flagging finance.

sam: +1 on notifying finance. also we should be careful with instance types: eu-west quotas only have limited a2-highgpu availability. maybe auto-fallback to g4dn if requested region lacks a2. put that as routing policy, not terraform change.

maria: good point — runtime will prefer a2 but module should expose allowed_instance_types list and a secondary fallback. will add validation in variables.tf: allowed_instance_types (list) and logic in launch template.

leo: one more gotcha: terraform provider upgrade from 4.x -> 5.x changed kms key id interpolation. If we bump provider in the same deploy as the module split we'll risk plan noise. recommend: provider bump in a separate PR, staged a day before module canary.

zara: can we add an automated smoke that provisions 1 GPU in a sandbox org with the new modules? terratest + ephemeral creds. That would catch kms/iam misconfigs earlier.

maria: yes — adding a sandbox job to ci pipeline. schedule: provider bump PR tomorrow, module split PR in 48h, canary deploy after sandbox success.

deploy-bot: CI: terraform fmt/validate passed. plan link: https://ci.internal/reports/1833001111/plan.html (canary target: us-west1).

sam: I'll open the finance FYI ticket and add the +8% temporary cost delta. also adding sig-ops rotation to monitor GPU quotas during canary.

leo: leaving a checklist comment in the PR: state backup snapshot, tfstate lock, manual approval gate, ops slack alert channel, rollback runbook with exact 'terraform apply -target=module.gpupool-core' steps.

zara: if anything fails we revert by pinning the previous module ref in the gitops repo and running a targeted destroy on the canary ASG. avoid running global destroy.

maria: perfect. I'll proceed with PRs and tag you all for review. thanks everyone :rocket:
